lessons.title: Listen and speak: describing people at work
lessons.objective: Describe a person and what he or she does in simple sentences.
lessons.course:
We describe people with simple words: She is tall. He is old. She has a basket.
We say their work: He is a farmer. She is a nurse. He is a tailor. She is a teacher.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
He is a farmer.
She is a nurse.
He has a hoe.

lessons.model: The adult shows a drawing: “This is Mr Mbah. He is a farmer. He is tall. He has a hoe.”
lessons.guided: Look at drawings of workers. For each one, say two sentences: what the person is, what he or she has.
lessons.exercise: Describe a farmer in one sentence.
lessons.answer: For example: He is a farmer. He has a hoe.
lessons.remediation: Use only “He is a …” or “She is a …” with three pictures.
lessons.transfer: Describe the work of one adult in your family.
lessons.materials: Drawings of workers (farmer, nurse, tailor, teacher, driver).

practice.prompt: Match each worker with a tool.
practice.answer: farmer: hoe; tailor: needle; teacher: chalk.
practice.explanation: Each worker uses tools.

practice.prompt: Listen and say after the voice.
practice.listen: She is a nurse. She works in a hospital.
practice.answer: She is a nurse. She works in a hospital.
practice.explanation: Say the whole sentence.

practice.prompt: Who works in a hospital?
practice.explanation: Nurses care for sick people in a hospital.

lessons.title: Read: sh and ch
lessons.objective: Read the digraphs sh and ch and words containing them.
lessons.course:
Two letters can make one sound. s and h together make sh, like when we ask for silence: shhh. c and h together make ch, like a train: ch, ch, ch.
Words: shop, fish, ship, chin, chop, rich.

support.title: Read with the adult
support.text:
sh: shop  fish  ship
ch: chin  chop  chip

lessons.model: The adult reads: “sh-o-p: shop. The tailor has a shop.” Then: “ch-o-p: chop. The cook chops onions.”
lessons.guided: Sort word cards into two groups: words with sh and words with ch. Read each word aloud.
lessons.exercise: Read the word: f – i – sh.
lessons.remediation: Say the sound sh several times with a finger on the lips, then read sh + one more sound.
lessons.transfer: Find a word with sh or ch on a shop sign or a box.
lessons.materials: Word cards with sh and ch.

practice.prompt: Which word has the sound sh?
practice.explanation: s and h make sh in ship.

practice.prompt: Complete with sh or ch.
practice.text: The fisherman sells fi[[sh]]. The cook [[ch]]ops onions.
practice.explanation: fish ends with sh; chop starts with ch.

practice.prompt: Put the sounds in order to make “shop”.
practice.explanation: sh is one sound made by two letters.

lessons.title: Write: letters n to z
lessons.objective: Form the small letters n to z from left to right, on the line.
lessons.course:
We finish the alphabet: n, o, p, q, r, s, t, u, v, w, x, y, z. The letters p, q and y go below the line. The letter t is a little tall.
Now we can write all the letters of the alphabet.

support.title: Trace with the adult
support.text:
n o p q r s t
u v w x y z

lessons.model: The adult writes p: “A stick down below the line, then round.” Then y: “A small v, then a tail below the line.”
lessons.guided: Trace each letter, then write it three times. Say its sound. Circle the letters that go below the line.
lessons.exercise: Write the letters p, q, y.
lessons.answer: p q y, with their tails below the line.
lessons.remediation: Practise the letters that go below the line with a coloured line under the writing line.
lessons.transfer: Write the name of a job: a tailor, a nurse.

practice.prompt: Write the letters r, s, t.
practice.answer: r s t, on the line.
practice.explanation: t is a little taller than r and s.

practice.prompt: Put the last letters of the alphabet in order.
practice.explanation: z is the last letter of the alphabet.

practice.prompt: Write the word “tailor”.
practice.explanation: t-a-i-l-o-r.

lessons.title: Action words: the simple present
lessons.objective: Use action verbs in the simple present with I, you, he and she.
lessons.course:
A verb is an action word: sell, cook, drive, sew.
With I, you, we and they, the verb does not change: I cook. They sell.
With he and she, we add s: He drives. She sews. The baker bakes bread.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
I cook. → She cooks.
I drive. → He drives.

lessons.model: The adult mimes and says: “I sew.” Then points to a picture: “The tailor sews.”
lessons.guided: Mime an action; the child says what you do with he or she and adds s.
lessons.remediation: Practise only with “she”: she cooks, she sells, she sings.
lessons.transfer: Say three things that people in your family do every day.

practice.prompt: Add the missing letter.
practice.text: She sell[[s]] fish. He cook[[s]] rice.
practice.answer: She sells fish. He cooks rice.
practice.explanation: With he and she, the verb takes s.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
practice.explanation: With he, add s: drives.

practice.prompt: Complete: The baker ___ (bake) bread.
practice.explanation: With the baker (he or she), add s.

lessons.title: Money: our coins up to 100 francs
lessons.objective: Recognise coins and pay small amounts up to 100 francs.
lessons.course:
We use coins of 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100 francs.
Two coins of 50 francs make 100 francs. Two coins of 25 francs make 50 francs.
We count the coins to pay the right amount.
lessons.model: At the shop, a pencil costs 50 francs. The adult pays with two coins of 25 francs: “25 and 25 make 50.”
lessons.guided: Play shop with real or paper coins. Pay for small things in different ways.
lessons.exercise: A sweet costs 25 francs. You pay with 50 francs. How much change do you get?
lessons.remediation: Use only coins of 50 and 100 francs at first.
lessons.transfer: With an adult, look at the coins in a purse and say their values.
lessons.materials: Coins or paper coins of 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100 francs.

practice.prompt: 50 francs + 50 francs = ? francs
practice.explanation: Two coins of 50 make 100 francs.

practice.prompt: Which coins make 30 francs?
Match each price with the coins.
practice.explanation: Add the coins.

lessons.title: Number bonds to 10
lessons.objective: Build the pairs of numbers that make 10 and use them to add quickly.
lessons.course:
Number bonds are pairs that make a number. The bonds of 10: 1 + 9, 2 + 8, 3 + 7, 4 + 6, 5 + 5.
If I know 6 + 4 = 10, I know 4 + 6 = 10 too.
lessons.model: The adult shows ten fingers, folds 3: “3 folded, 7 standing. 3 and 7 make 10.”
lessons.guided: Use ten bottle tops in two hands. Move some from one hand to the other and say the bond each time.
lessons.remediation: Use ten fingers to see each bond.
lessons.transfer: Play with a friend: one says a number, the other says what makes 10.

practice.explanation: 6 and 4 make 10.

practice.prompt: Match the numbers that make 10.
practice.explanation: Each pair makes 10.

practice.prompt: Complete the bonds.
practice.explanation: Think: what is missing to make 10?

lessons.title: Adding up to 50
lessons.objective: Add numbers up to 50 using tens and units, and solve simple problems about work.
lessons.course: To add 23 + 14, we add the tens and the units: 2 tens + 1 ten = 3 tens; 3 units + 4 units = 7 units. 23 + 14 = 37.
lessons.model: A tailor sews 20 shirts on Monday and 15 on Tuesday. The adult adds: “20 + 15: 3 tens and 5 units: 35 shirts.”
lessons.guided: Make each number with bundles and sticks, put them together, then count the tens and the units.
lessons.exercise: A farmer picks 21 cocoa pods, then 12 more. How many pods?
lessons.remediation: Add a number of tens first (20 + 10), then add numbers with units.
lessons.transfer: Make up a problem about a job you know and solve it.
lessons.materials: Bundles of ten sticks, loose sticks.

practice.explanation: 3 tens + 1 ten = 4 tens; 2 + 5 = 7 units: 47.

practice.prompt: A carpenter makes 10 chairs and then 20 chairs. How many chairs?
Complete.
practice.explanation: Add tens with tens, units with units.

lessons.title: Straight lines and curved lines
lessons.objective: Recognise and draw straight lines and curved lines, and make shapes and letters with them.
lessons.course:
A straight line does not bend, like the edge of a ruler. A curved line bends, like a rainbow.
Shapes and letters are made of lines: a triangle has three straight lines; the letter C is a curve.
lessons.model: The adult shows the tools of workers: “The ruler of the carpenter is straight. The rim of the basin is curved.”
lessons.guided: With a string, make a straight line, then a curved line. Draw both in sand, then on paper.
lessons.exercise: Is the letter O made of straight lines or curved lines?
lessons.remediation: Trace straight and curved lines on a model before drawing them alone.
lessons.transfer: Find three straight lines and three curved lines in your house.

practice.prompt: Which letter has only straight lines?
practice.explanation: L is made of two straight lines.

practice.prompt: Draw a straight line and a curved line.
practice.answer: One straight line and one curved line.
practice.explanation: Use a ruler for the straight line.

practice.prompt: Match each thing with its kind of line.
practice.answer: ruler: straight; rainbow: curved; door edge: straight.
practice.explanation: A straight line does not bend.

lessons.title: Tools and machines people use
lessons.objective: Identify common tools and machines in the locality and say what they are used for.
lessons.course:
People use tools and machines to work. A hoe digs the soil. A cutlass cuts grass. A hammer drives nails. A sewing machine sews clothes. A grinding machine grinds corn.
We use tools carefully and only with an adult.
lessons.model: The carpenter uses a hammer and a saw. The tailor uses a sewing machine. The farmer uses a hoe.
lessons.guided: Look at pictures of tools. Say the name of each tool and mime its use.
lessons.exercise: Which tool does the farmer use to dig?
lessons.remediation: Use three real or drawn tools and their use first.
lessons.transfer: Find a tool or a machine used in your house and say what it does.
lessons.materials: Pictures of tools and machines; safe real objects if possible.

practice.prompt: Match each tool with its use.
practice.answer: hammer: nails; hoe: soil; sewing machine: clothes.
practice.explanation: Each tool has a use.

practice.prompt: Who uses a saw?
practice.explanation: The carpenter cuts wood with a saw.

practice.prompt: Why do we use tools only with an adult?
practice.explanation: Many tools are sharp or heavy.

lessons.title: Ma, pa, la : les premières syllabes
lessons.objective: Lire les consonnes m, p, l, t avec une voyelle pour former des syllabes et des mots courts.
lessons.course:
Une consonne et une voyelle font une syllabe : m + a = ma ; p + a = pa ; l + a = la ; t + o = to.
Avec deux syllabes, on lit un mot : ma-man (maman), pa-pa (papa), to-ma-te (tomate).

support.title: Lis avec l’adulte
support.text:
ma  pa  la  to
papa  maman  tomate

lessons.model: L’adulte lit : « p… a… pa ; pa… pa… papa ! » Le papa de Bih est tailleur.
lessons.guided: Avec des cartes, assemble une consonne et une voyelle. Lis la syllabe. Puis assemble deux syllabes pour lire un mot.
lessons.remediation: Reste sur une consonne (m) avec toutes les voyelles : ma, me, mi, mo, mu.
lessons.transfer: Lis « papa » et « maman » sur une carte et offre-la à tes parents.
lessons.materials: Cartes de lettres et de syllabes.

practice.prompt: Remets les syllabes dans l’ordre pour lire « tomate ».
practice.explanation: On lit de gauche à droite.

practice.prompt: Complète le mot.
practice.explanation: ma-man : maman.

practice.prompt: Quelle syllabe fait m + a ?
practice.explanation: m puis a : ma.

lessons.title: Being honest and sharing
lessons.objective: Show honesty and sharing in daily life.
lessons.course:
An honest person tells the truth and does not take what belongs to others. If we find something, we give it back.
Sharing means giving part of what we have to others: food, toys, our time.
lessons.model: At the market, a seller gives Tabi too much change. Tabi gives the extra money back. The seller says: “Thank you, you are honest.”
lessons.guided: Listen to short situations and say what an honest child does. Share a snack equally with a friend.
lessons.exercise: You find a pen that is not yours. What do you do?
lessons.answer: I give it back to its owner or to the teacher.
accept: I give it back to its owner or to the teacher
lessons.remediation: Use real objects: find, ask “Whose is it?”, give back.
lessons.transfer: Share something with someone at home today.
lessons.materials: Small objects, a snack to share.

practice.prompt: Which child is honest?
choices: Bih gives back a lost purse.
practice.answer: Bih gives back a lost purse.
practice.explanation: An honest person gives back what is not his.

practice.prompt: Share 6 groundnuts equally between 2 friends. How many each?
practice.explanation: Sharing equally: 3 each.

practice.prompt: What does an honest person always tell?
practice.explanation: Being honest means telling the truth.

lessons.title: The craftsman and his tools
lessons.objective: Identify the tools of some craftsmen and show interest in craftsmanship.
lessons.course:
A craftsman makes things with his hands. The carpenter uses a saw, a hammer and a plane. The tailor uses scissors, a needle and a tape measure. The basket maker uses raffia and a knife.
Craftsmen keep their tools clean and safe.
lessons.model: In the workshop, the carpenter shows Ayuk his saw and says: “I always keep it in its place.”
lessons.guided: Look at pictures of craftsmen and their tools. Match each tool with its craftsman.
lessons.remediation: Work with two craftsmen the child has seen.
lessons.transfer: Visit a craftsman near your house with an adult and name two of his tools.

practice.prompt: Match each tool with its craftsman.
practice.answer: saw: carpenter; scissors: tailor; raffia: basket maker.
practice.explanation: Each craftsman has his tools.

practice.prompt: What does a craftsman use to make things?
practice.explanation: Craftsmen work with their hands.

practice.prompt: Say one thing a carpenter makes.
practice.answer: For example: a chair, a table, a door.
practice.explanation: Carpenters make things with wood.

lessons.title: Painting with colours from nature
lessons.objective: Identify painting materials and produce paint from local materials.
lessons.course:
Long ago, and still today, artists make paint with things from nature: charcoal gives black, red earth (clay) gives red or brown, white clay (kaolin) gives white, crushed leaves give green.
We mix the powder with a little water and paint with a brush or a stick with cotton.
lessons.model: The adult crushes charcoal, adds a few drops of water and paints a line: “Black paint from charcoal.”
lessons.guided: With the adult, make two colours from nature. Paint a simple picture on cardboard.
lessons.remediation: Use one colour only, then add a second.
lessons.transfer: Look for other things at home that can give colour (turmeric, hibiscus…) with an adult.
lessons.materials: Charcoal, red earth, white clay, leaves, water, cardboard, a brush or a stick with cotton.

practice.prompt: Match each material with its colour.
practice.answer: charcoal: black; white clay: white; leaves: green.
practice.explanation: Nature gives many colours.

practice.prompt: What do we add to the powder to make paint?
practice.explanation: Water turns the powder into paint.

practice.prompt: Draw what you painted.
practice.explanation: Show the colours you used.

lessons.title: Throwing a ball with good posture
lessons.objective: Handle objects of different weights and throw them with good posture.
lessons.course:
To throw well: stand with one foot in front, look at the target, bring the arm back, then throw and follow with the arm.
We throw only when nobody is in front of us.
lessons.model: The adult shows: left foot in front, arm back, throw. The ball goes far into the basket.
lessons.guided: Throw a light ball into a basket from close, then from farther. Then throw a heavier object (a bean bag).
lessons.exercise: Where do we look when we throw?
lessons.remediation: Throw a big soft ball with two hands first.
lessons.transfer: Play throwing bottle tops into a box at home.
lessons.materials: Balls, bean bags, a basket or a box.

practice.prompt: Put the steps of a throw in order.
practice.explanation: A good posture makes a good throw.

practice.prompt: When can we throw?
choices: when nobody is in front of us
practice.answer: when nobody is in front of us
practice.explanation: Safety first.

practice.prompt: Ayuk throws 6 balls. 4 go into the basket. How many miss?

lessons.title: Traditional occupations of my village
lessons.objective: Use appropriate words to describe traditional occupations of the locality and show love for culture.
lessons.course:
In villages, people do traditional work: farming, fishing, hunting, weaving baskets, making pots, carving wood, palm wine tapping, blacksmithing.
Each occupation has its tools and its words in the local language.
lessons.model: Grandfather Ndi shows Tabi how he weaves a basket with raffia and says the name of the basket in his language.
lessons.guided: Ask an elder about a traditional occupation of your family or village. Learn the name of one tool in the family language.
lessons.exercise: Name a traditional occupation of your area.
lessons.answer: For example: farming, fishing, weaving, pottery, carving.
lessons.transfer: Draw a person doing a traditional occupation and say its name in your language.

practice.prompt: Match each occupation with what is made.
practice.answer: weaving: basket; pottery: pot; carving: stool.
practice.explanation: Each craft makes different things.

practice.prompt: Which one is a traditional occupation?
practice.explanation: Fishing with a canoe is a traditional occupation.

practice.prompt: Ask an elder: what is the name of a hoe in your family language? Say it.
practice.answer: The word for hoe in the family language.
practice.explanation: Every language has words for tools.

lessons.title: Using the keyboard and the mouse
lessons.objective: Describe how we use the keyboard and the mouse.
lessons.course:
On the keyboard, each key has a letter, a number or a sign. We press one key at a time with one finger. The long key is the space bar: it puts a space between words.
We hold the mouse gently, we move it on the table, and we click with one finger.
lessons.model: Ayuk types his name on a computer, letter by letter, then presses the space bar.
lessons.guided: On a real keyboard or a paper keyboard, find the letters of your name and press them in order.
lessons.exercise: Which key puts a space between two words?
lessons.remediation: Find the first letter of the name only.
lessons.transfer: With an adult, type your name on a phone or a computer.
lessons.materials: A keyboard or a printed paper keyboard.

practice.prompt: Put the letters of the name “Bih” in the order to type them.
practice.explanation: We type letter by letter, from left to right.

practice.prompt: How do we click with the mouse?
practice.explanation: The mouse is fragile.

practice.prompt: How many keys do you press to type “CAT”?
practice.explanation: C, A, T: 3 keys.
